observed_authority.proposition: Hybrid PACs may solicit and accept unlimited funds into a segregated non-contribution account for independent expenditures, other federal-candidate-referencing ads, and generic voter drives, while maintaining a separate contribution account subject to statutory source and amount restrictions.

For a Hybrid PAC non-contribution account, unlimited receipts must be segregated from source-restricted and amount-limited candidate-contribution funds; both accounts are subject to FEC reporting guidance and account-specific expense allocation.

Super PACs and Hybrid PAC non-contribution accounts may accept unlimited contributions from individuals, corporations, labor organizations, and other political committees, but not from foreign nationals, federal contractors, national banks, or federally chartered corporations.

An independent expenditure expressly advocates election or defeat of a clearly identified candidate and is not made in coordination with a candidate, campaign, or political party; coordination can convert a communication into an in-kind contribution subject to contribution limits and, for prohibited-source funding, a prohibited contribution.

A Hybrid PAC may not use funds from its non-contribution account to make a contribution to a federal candidate; any candidate contributions must come from the contribution account and comply with applicable limits and source restrictions.
